correctness.rationale: The six support-function inequalities are necessary and sufficient by linear-programming duality; every possible dual basic feasible distribution (support size at most four among eight sign vectors) was enumerated exactly as four opposite pairs and two parity quartets. For any frame of fitting radius at most 3/2 all seven nonempty subset sums have integral l1 norm at most three, bounding the possible columns to 62. Exhaustive integer arithmetic proves the 1264->928 filter, index histogram and all 23 symmetry orbits. A separate complete radius-below-3/2 test over the 24 integral columns with l1 norm at most two, using opposite pair sums at most two and parity sums at most five, returns zero, and the standard basis attains 3/2. No heuristic or incomplete numerical search is involved; all important ranges and code are included in the standalone package.

value.rationale: For an explicitly introduced invariant with a sharp 2026 octahedral determinant theorem, classifying every optimal integer Kuhn frame is a natural structural next question, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The index-three gap, 928 count, and 23 symmetry orbits distinguish proper-sublattice optimal packets from basis optimizers and quantify a surprising nonmonotone index spectrum that cannot be read from the previously known determinant ceiling. The invariant matters for lattice covering via common-frame triangulations.
